DECISION. Split dph_sh_covectorEuclideanNorm_interior_le (depth 5 < max_depth 6) into 4 children: 1 new theorem and 3 comparator-accepted declarations reused by name with byte-identical frozen types, titles and statements.

WHY. The supplied proof has two layers.
- Steps 4–8 bound the Euclidean coefficient norm of the contraction γ_w = γ(w, ·) by √(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ|, using Cauchy–Schwarz in the first slot, reindexing by Fin.consEquiv, the all-tuples identity and cancelling k!. This estimate does not involve a, T or m. Nothing in the pinned project, SimonGMT, Mathlib or the DAG provides it; Mathlib's norm_curryLeft is the operator-norm identity. It is the one genuinely new obligation and becomes the leaf contraction_bound.
- Steps 1–3 and 9 only assemble homogeneity, the pull-back bound and that estimate.
Homogeneity (step 2) is exactly the accepted declaration fiw_tb_ext_covectorNorm_smul, so it is reused rather than re-proved; its candidate adds one 14-line theorem to the frozen base. pullback_norm and tuple_sum_factorial are already resolved dependencies of this node. Listing them as reused children lets contraction_bound declare its sibling dependency and lets the assembly cite pullback_norm; the DAG already has 16 such dependency/child overlaps. Splitting further (the Cauchy–Schwarz line or the reindexing) would give non-reusable fragments. Not splitting would re-prove homogeneity and leave the core estimate unnamed.

CHILDREN ↔ SUPPLIED PROOF.
- norm_smul = fiw_tb_ext_covectorNorm_smul (node root.flat_iff_weak-a1.total_boundedness-a1.extend-a1.norm_smul-a1, candidate 47d3d707): step 2.

HOW THE CHILDREN GIVE THE SELECTED STATEMENT (steps 1, 2, 3 and 9 stay in this node). Assume β(v) = a·γ(Fin.cons w (i ↦ T(v_i))) for all v.
(1) Put δ := γ.curryLeft w. Then δ(u) = γ(Matrix.vecCons w u) = γ(Fin.cons w u) for all u (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply; this holds definitionally). So contraction_bound gives |δ| ≤ √(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ|.
(2) β = a • δ.compContinuousLinearMap T: at every v both sides equal a·γ(Fin.cons w (i ↦ T(v_i))) (ext, smul_apply, compContinuousLinearMap_apply).
(3) norm_smul gives |β| = |a|·|δ.compContinuousLinearMap T|. pullback_norm (P := m, Q := m′, j := k, L := T, α := δ) gives |δ.compContinuousLinearMap T| ≤ ‖T‖^k·|δ|.
(4) Multiplying by |a| ≥ 0 and ‖T‖^k ≥ 0: |β| ≤ |a|·‖T‖^k·|δ| ≤ |a|·‖T‖^k·√(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ| = |a|·√(k+1)·‖w‖·‖T‖^k·|γ|.

subproblems.title: Homogeneity of the Euclidean coefficient norm: |cα| = |c|·|α|
subproblems.statement: For all P, q ∈ ℕ, every c ∈ ℝ and every q-covector α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) q: covectorEuclideanNorm (c • α) = |c| · covectorEuclideanNorm α. Here covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin q → Fin P} t_I(α)), where t_I(α) = α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(q−1)})² if I is strictly increasing and t_I(α) = 0 otherwise, and e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i.

In the verbatim text below, 'the parent proof' and 'step 4(a)' refer to the proof of that node's own parent (root.flat_iff_weak-a1.total_boundedness-a1.extend-a1); the numbered argument does not depend on them. Source: the homogeneity fact |tα| = |t|·|α| stated in the Notation paragraph and used in step 4(a) of the parent proof. It is also step 1 of the accepted proof of br_la_abs_apply_le_mul_mass.

1. Scalar multiplication of continuous alternating maps is pointwise (ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply). So for every I : Fin q → Fin P, (c • α)(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(q−1)}) = c·α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(q−1)}).
   - For strictly increasing I: t_I(c • α) = (c·α(e_I))² = c²·t_I(α) (mul_pow).
   - For the other I: t_I(c • α) = 0 = c²·t_I(α).
2. Summing over the finitely many I gives Σ_I t_I(c • α) = c²·s, where s := Σ_I t_I(α) ≥ 0 (Finset.mul_sum).
3. Therefore:
   covectorEuclideanNorm (c • α) = √(c²·s)
   = √(c²)·√s (Real.sqrt_mul, as c² ≥ 0)
   = |c|·√s (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs)
   = |c|·covectorEuclideanNorm α. ∎

Reference Lean proof (kernel-checked in a scratch build importing GMT.Ch06.Submission, in the comparator's contract scope; sibling dependencies are referenced as Submission.X):
theorem Submission.fiw_tb_ext_covectorNorm_smul : ∀ (P q : ℕ) (c : ℝ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) q), covectorEuclideanNorm (c • α) = |c| * covectorEuclideanNorm α := by
  intro P q c α
  unfold covectorEuclideanNorm
  rw [← Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs, ← Real.sqrt_mul (sq_nonneg c), Finset.mul_sum]
  congr 1
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun I _ => ?_
  split_ifs
  · simp only [ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_pow]
  · simp
proof_key_steps: (c•α)(e_I) = c·α(e_I), so each squared coefficient is multiplied by c².
Factor c² out of the finite sum.

Source: fact (F3) of the parent proof. The parent justifies (F3) by the singular value decomposition. Transferring that argument to covectorEuclideanNorm, which is defined on continuous alternating maps through the standard basis, would need an SVD factorization L = Σ_i σ_i u_i ⊗ v_i and the orthonormality, for this norm, of the wedges of an arbitrary orthonormal basis. The pinned Mathlib has singular values (LinearMap.singularValues) and an inner product on the abstract exterior power ⋀[ℝ]^n E, but neither the factorization nor any link to covectorEuclideanNorm. The same inequality is therefore proved by the elementary tensor (Hilbert–Schmidt) argument below, which uses only the standard bases.

Notation:
- e_1, …, e_P and e′_1, …, e′_Q are the standard orthonormal bases of ℝ^P and ℝ^Q (EuclideanSpace.basisFun);
- for i : Fin j → Fin P, e∘i := (e_{i(1)}, …, e_{i(j)}), and similarly e′∘i for i : Fin j → Fin Q;
- |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ, so for a j-covector γ on ℝ^m (m ∈ {P, Q}, with the corresponding standard basis), |γ|² = Σ_{I : Fin j → Fin m strictly increasing} γ(e∘I)²;
- L^#α := α.compContinuousLinearMap L, so (L^#α)(v₁, …, v_j) = α(Lv₁, …, Lv_j);
- |·| on vectors is the Euclidean norm, ⟨·,·⟩ the inner product, and ‖L‖ the operator norm.

1. (Sum over all index tuples.) For every j-covector γ on ℝ^m: Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin m} γ(e∘i)² = j!·|γ|².
   (a) If i is not injective, e∘i has two equal entries, so γ(e∘i) = 0 because γ is alternating.
   (b) The map (I, σ) ↦ I ∘ σ is a bijection from pairs (I strictly increasing Fin j → Fin m, σ a permutation of Fin j) onto the injective maps Fin j → Fin m.
      - Surjectivity: for injective i, the tuple i ∘ (sort i) is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort) and injective, hence strictly increasing. With I := i ∘ sort i and σ := (sort i)⁻¹, I ∘ σ = i.
      - Injectivity: if I ∘ σ = I′ ∘ σ′, then range I = range I′. A strictly increasing map Fin j → Fin m is determined by its range (it enumerates the range in increasing order), so I = I′, and then σ = σ′ because I is injective.
   (c) For such pairs, γ(e∘(I ∘ σ)) = sign(σ)·γ(e∘I) (AlternatingMap.map_perm), so γ(e∘(I ∘ σ))² = γ(e∘I)².
   By (a)–(c), Σ_i γ(e∘i)² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} Σ_σ γ(e∘I)² = j!·Σ_I γ(e∘I)² = j!·|γ|², because Fin j has j! permutations.
2. (One slot.) For every linear functional λ : ℝ^Q → ℝ: Σ_{a=1}^{P} λ(Le_a)² ≤ ‖L‖²·Σ_{b=1}^{Q} λ(e′_b)².
   - Put g := Σ_b λ(e′_b)e′_b ∈ ℝ^Q. Then λ(y) = ⟨g, y⟩ for every y (expand y = Σ_b ⟨e′_b, y⟩e′_b), and |g|² = Σ_b λ(e′_b)².
   - Put u := Σ_a λ(Le_a)e_a ∈ ℝ^P. Then |u|² = Σ_a λ(Le_a)², and by linearity λ(Lu) = Σ_a λ(Le_a)² = |u|².
   - By Cauchy–Schwarz, |u|² = ⟨g, Lu⟩ ≤ |g|·|Lu| ≤ |g|·‖L‖·|u|.
   Hence |u| ≤ ‖L‖·|g| (trivial if u = 0, otherwise divide by |u|), and squaring gives the claim.
3. (All slots, by induction on j.) For every j ∈ ℕ and every j-multilinear map β : (ℝ^Q)^j → ℝ:
   Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin P} β(Le_{i(1)}, …, Le_{i(j)})² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin Q} β(e′∘i)².
   For j = 0 both sides equal β()², because there is exactly one empty tuple and ‖L‖⁰ = 1.
   For the step j → j + 1, write tuples as i = Fin.cons a i′ with a ∈ Fin P and i′ : Fin j → Fin P (and likewise over Fin Q). Write Le∘i′ := (Le_{i′(1)}, …, Le_{i′(j)}).
   - For fixed a, the induction hypothesis applied to the j-multilinear map β(Le_a, ·) gives Σ_{i′} β(Le_a, Le∘i′)² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i″ : Fin j → Fin Q} β(Le_a, e′∘i″)².
   - Summing over a, the left sides add up to Σ_{i : Fin (j+1) → Fin P} β(Le_{i(1)}, …, Le_{i(j+1)})². After exchanging the finite sums, the right sides add up to ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i″} Σ_a λ_{i″}(Le_a)², where λ_{i″}(y) := β(y, e′∘i″) is a linear functional on ℝ^Q.
   - By step 2, this is at most ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i″} ‖L‖²·Σ_b β(e′_b, e′∘i″)² = ‖L‖^{2(j+1)}·Σ_{i : Fin (j+1) → Fin Q} β(e′∘i)².
   This proves the claim for j + 1.
4. (Conclusion.) Apply step 3 to β := α, an alternating and in particular multilinear map. Since (L^#α)(e∘i) = α(Le_{i(1)}, …, Le_{i(j)}), this gives
   Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin P} (L^#α)(e∘i)² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin Q} α(e′∘i)².
   By step 1, applied to L^#α on ℝ^P and to α on ℝ^Q, this reads j!·|L^#α|² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·j!·|α|². Dividing by j! > 0 gives |L^#α|² ≤ (‖L‖^j·|α|)². Both |L^#α| and ‖L‖^j·|α| are nonnegative, so |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^j·|α|.
   No restriction on j, P, Q is used. For j = 0 both sides equal |α()|; if j > P or j > Q, the corresponding sums over strictly increasing indices are empty. ∎
proof_key_steps: For an alternating γ, the sum of γ(e∘i)² over all index tuples equals j!·|γ|²: non-injective tuples give 0, and injective ones are uniquely permutations of increasing ones.
Single-slot bound Σ_a λ(L e_a)² ≤ ‖L‖² Σ_b λ(e′_b)², via the Riesz vector g of λ, u = Σ_a λ(Le_a)e_a and Cauchy–Schwarz.
Induction over the j slots of a multilinear map gives Σ_i α(L e∘i)² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j} Σ_i α(e′∘i)².
Divide by j! and take square roots: |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^j |α|.

Provenance (for information only; nothing below depends on it): this is step 1 of the proof supplied for the parent theorem iwl_sp_covectorEuclideanNorm_pullback_le, with all details filled in.

Notation. Fix m, j ∈ ℕ and γ ∈ Covector (Eucl m) j, a continuous alternating j-linear map (ℝ^m)^j → ℝ.
- e_c := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin m) ℝ c (c ∈ Fin m) is the standard basis.
- For i : Fin j → Fin m, e∘i := (k ↦ e_{i(k)}) : Fin j → ℝ^m and F(i) := γ(e∘i)².
- S := {I : Fin j → Fin m // StrictMono I} is a finite type, and Perm(Fin j) is the finite group of permutations of Fin j.
- |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ.
The claim is Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin m} F(i) = j!·|γ|².

1. (The squared norm.) By definition |γ| = √N with N := Σ_{I : Fin j → Fin m} t_I, where t_I := F(I) if I is strictly increasing and t_I := 0 otherwise.
   - Every t_I ≥ 0, so N ≥ 0 and |γ|² = (√N)² = N (Real.sq_sqrt).
   - Dropping the zero terms, N = Σ_{I ∈ univ.filter StrictMono} F(I) = Σ_{I : S} F(I) (Finset.sum_filter, Finset.sum_subtype).
   Hence |γ|² = Σ_{I : S} F(I).
2. (Non-injective tuples contribute 0.) Let i be non-injective, say i(a) = i(b) with a ≠ b.
   - Then e∘i takes the same value e_{i(a)} = e_{i(b)} at the positions a ≠ b, so e∘i is not injective.
   - γ(e∘i) = 0 because γ is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective).
   Hence F(i) = 0.
3. (Permutation invariance.) Let i : Fin j → Fin m and σ ∈ Perm(Fin j).
   - e∘(i∘σ) = (e∘i)∘σ, and γ((e∘i)∘σ) = sign(σ)·γ(e∘i) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to γ.toAlternatingMap).
   - sign(σ) ∈ {1, −1} (Int.units_eq_one_or), so squaring gives F(i∘σ) = F(i).
4. (Parametrization of the injective tuples.) Define Φ : S × Perm(Fin j) → (Fin j → Fin m) by Φ(I, σ) := I∘σ.
   (a) Φ is injective. Suppose I∘σ = I′∘σ′ with I, I′ strictly increasing.
      - σ and σ′ are bijections, so range I = range(I∘σ) = range(I′∘σ′) = range I′ (EquivLike.range_comp).
      - Two strictly increasing maps on the well-order Fin j with the same range are equal (StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so I = I′.
      - Then I(σ(k)) = I(σ′(k)) for every k. Since I is strictly increasing, it is injective, so σ(k) = σ′(k) for all k, that is, σ = σ′.
   (b) Every injective i is a value of Φ. Let τ := Tuple.sort i ∈ Perm(Fin j).
      - i∘τ is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort).
      - i∘τ is injective, as a composition of injective maps.
      - A monotone injective map between linear orders is strictly increasing (Monotone.strictMono_of_injective), so I := i∘τ ∈ S.
      - Φ(I, τ⁻¹) = i∘τ∘τ⁻¹ = i.
5. (Reindexing.) Let A := Finset.image Φ univ, the set of values of Φ.
   (a) Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin m} F(i) = Σ_{i ∈ A} F(i). For i ∉ A, i is not injective by 4(b), so F(i) = 0 by step 2 (Finset.sum_subset).
   (b) Σ_{i ∈ A} F(i) = Σ_{(I,σ) ∈ S × Perm(Fin j)} F(I∘σ), because Φ is injective by 4(a) (Finset.sum_image).
   (c) By step 3, F(I∘σ) = F(I) for each pair. So the sum equals Σ_{I : S} Σ_{σ ∈ Perm(Fin j)} F(I) (Fintype.sum_prod_type), which is Σ_{I : S} |Perm(Fin j)|·F(I).
   (d) |Perm(Fin j)| = (card (Fin j))! = j! (Fintype.card_perm, Fintype.card_fin). So the sum equals j!·Σ_{I : S} F(I).
6. (Conclusion.) Combining steps 5 and 1: Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin m} F(i) = j!·Σ_{I : S} F(I) = j!·|γ|².
   No restriction on m or j was used:
   - for j = 0, S consists of the empty tuple and Perm(Fin 0) has 1 = 0! element;
   - for j > m, S is empty and there are no injective tuples, so both sides are 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: |γ|² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} F(I) with F(i) = γ(e∘i)². This follows from Real.sq_sqrt of the nonnegative defining sum, after dropping the zero terms.
F vanishes on non-injective tuples because γ is alternating (map_eq_zero_of_not_injective).
F(i∘σ) = F(i) for every permutation σ (AlternatingMap.map_perm, with sign(σ)² = 1).
Φ(I, σ) = I∘σ is injective on {strictly increasing I} × Perm(Fin j) (by equal ranges and StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT). It hits every injective tuple, via Tuple.sort and Tuple.monotone_sort.
Reindex: Σ_i F(i) = Σ_{(I,σ)} F(I∘σ) = Σ_I j!·F(I) = j!·|γ|² (Fintype.card_perm).

subproblems.title: Contraction bound |γ(w, ·)| ≤ √(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ| for the Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblems.statement: Let p, k ∈ ℕ, let γ be a (k+1)-covector on ℝ^p (γ : Covector (Eucl p) (k+1), a continuous alternating (k+1)-linear map (ℝ^p)^{k+1} → ℝ), let w ∈ ℝ^p, and let δ be a k-covector on ℝ^p (δ : Covector (Eucl p) k) with δ(u) = γ(Fin.cons w u) = γ(w, u_1, …, u_k) for every u : Fin k → ℝ^p. Then |δ| ≤ √(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ|. Here |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm, the Euclidean norm of the coefficients α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}) over strictly increasing index tuples I (e = standard basis of ℝ^p, EuclideanSpace.basisFun), and ‖w‖ is the Euclidean norm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (p k : ℕ) (γ : Covector (Eucl p) (k + 1)) (w : Eucl p) (δ : Covector (Eucl p) k), (∀ u : Fin k → Eucl p, δ u = γ (Fin.cons w u)) → covectorEuclideanNorm δ ≤ Real.sqrt ((k : ℝ) + 1) * ‖w‖ * covectorEuclideanNorm γ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–8 of the supplied proof of the selected parent dph_sh_covectorEuclideanNorm_interior_le (the bound for the contraction γ_w := γ(w, ·) inside fact (F8) of dph_smooth_homotopy), extracted with all details filled in. The contraction is represented by an arbitrary k-covector δ with δ(u) = γ(Fin.cons w u), so the statement does not fix a construction such as ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft. Sibling used: tuple_sum_factorial (iwl_sp_pn_sum_sq_tuples_eq_factorial_mul).

Notation: for an n-covector α on ℝ^p, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin p strictly increasing} α(e∘I)²), where e_b := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin p) ℝ b is the standard basis of ℝ^p and e∘I := (i ↦ e_{I(i)}). For w ∈ ℝ^p, w_b is its b-th coordinate. Fix p, k, γ, w and δ as in the statement, so δ(u) = γ(Fin.cons w u) for every u : Fin k → ℝ^p.

1. (Expansion in the first slot.) w = Σ_b w_b·e_b (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr for EuclideanSpace.basisFun, whose coordinates are the w_b by EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr). For fixed u : Fin k → ℝ^p, the map x ↦ γ(Fin.cons x u) is linear in x. Indeed it is x ↦ (γ.curryLeft x)(u): ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft γ is a continuous linear map, and (γ.curryLeft x)(u) = γ(Matrix.vecCons x u) = γ(Fin.cons x u) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply; Matrix.vecCons is Fin.cons). Equivalently, γ is linear in its first argument (ContinuousAlternatingMap.cons_add, cons_smul). With the hypothesis on δ this gives, for every u,
   δ(u) = γ(Fin.cons w u) = Σ_b w_b·γ(Fin.cons e_b u).
2. (Basis tuples.) For b ∈ Fin p and J : Fin k → Fin p, Fin.cons e_b (e∘J) = e∘(Fin.cons b J) as maps Fin (k+1) → ℝ^p. At the entry 0 both sides equal e_b (Fin.cons_zero). At an entry i.succ both sides equal e_{J(i)} (Fin.cons_succ). Every entry has one of these two forms (Fin.cases). Step 1 with u := e∘J therefore gives δ(e∘J) = Σ_b w_b·γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J)).
3. (Cauchy–Schwarz.) Fix J : Fin k → Fin p. By step 2 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for finite sums (Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq):
   δ(e∘J)² = (Σ_b w_b·γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J)))² ≤ (Σ_b w_b²)·Σ_b γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J))² = ‖w‖²·Σ_b γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J))²,
   using ‖w‖² = Σ_b w_b² (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq).
4. (Reindexing.) The map (b, J) ↦ Fin.cons b J is a bijection Fin p × (Fin k → Fin p) → (Fin (k+1) → Fin p) (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ => Fin p)). Exchange the two finite sums (Finset.sum_comm), combine them into one sum over pairs (Fintype.sum_prod_type') and reindex along this bijection (Fintype.sum_equiv, or Equiv.sum_comp). This gives
   Σ_{J : Fin k → Fin p} Σ_b γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J))² = Σ_{I : Fin (k+1) → Fin p} γ(e∘I)².
5. (Summation and the all-tuples identity.) tuple_sum_factorial with m := p gives, for δ in degree j := k and for γ in degree j := k+1:
   Σ_{J : Fin k → Fin p} δ(e∘J)² = k!·|δ|² and Σ_{I : Fin (k+1) → Fin p} γ(e∘I)² = (k+1)!·|γ|².
   Sum step 3 over all J (Finset.sum_le_sum), pull the constant ‖w‖² out of the sum (Finset.mul_sum) and use step 4:
   k!·|δ|² = Σ_J δ(e∘J)² ≤ ‖w‖²·Σ_J Σ_b γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J))² = ‖w‖²·Σ_I γ(e∘I)² = ‖w‖²·(k+1)!·|γ|².
6. (Cancelling k!.) Since (k+1)! = (k+1)·k! (Nat.factorial_succ), step 5 reads k!·|δ|² ≤ k!·((k+1)·‖w‖²·|γ|²). As k! > 0 (Nat.factorial_pos), this gives |δ|² ≤ (k+1)·‖w‖²·|γ|² (le_of_mul_le_mul_left).
7. (Square roots.) Since k+1 ≥ 0, (√(k+1))² = k+1 (Real.sq_sqrt), so (k+1)·‖w‖²·|γ|² = (√(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ|)². Both |δ| and √(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ| are ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg, Real.sqrt_nonneg, norm_nonneg). Hence |δ|² ≤ (√(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ|)² gives |δ| ≤ √(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ| (pow_le_pow_iff_left₀ with exponent 2 ≠ 0).
No restriction on p or k is used. For k = 0 there is exactly one tuple J (the empty one), 0! = 1, and step 2 only concerns the entry 0. For p = 0 we have w = 0, and all sums over Fin p are empty, so δ(e∘J) = 0 for every J and both sides of the bound are 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Linearity of γ in its first slot (w = Σ_b w_b e_b, curryLeft) and Fin.cons e_b (e∘J) = e∘(Fin.cons b J) give δ(e∘J) = Σ_b w_b·γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J)).
Summing over J and reindexing by Fin.consEquiv: Σ_J δ(e∘J)² ≤ ‖w‖²·Σ_{I : Fin (k+1) → Fin p} γ(e∘I)².
tuple_sum_factorial turns this into k!|δ|² ≤ ‖w‖²(k+1)!|γ|². Cancel k! > 0 using (k+1)! = (k+1)·k!, then take nonnegative square roots: |δ| ≤ √(k+1)‖w‖|γ|.
